name: s6_revert_by_reference
source_note: Hand-built stateful project: notes, a tiny JSONL-backed notes CLI (add/list/find). Eight dependent turns add tags, created_at + list --since, tag normalization (lowercase + strip + internal-whitespace-runs -> '-') on write AND query, archive/unarchive with --all, a case-insensitive search whose tag matching piggybacks on that normalization, a REVERT of the normalization phrased by historical reference (complete removal of the cleanup logic demanded, including docs/tests; raw tags again, but the later search behavior must survive), rename-tag operating on raw tags, and finally an opt-in --normalize-tags flag that must reproduce the removed semantics exactly. No third-party deps; Python stdlib only.
discriminator: Turns 6 and 8 address earlier work by reference instead of restating it. Turn 6 ('that tag cleanup we added a while back ... take it back out ... tags should go back to working the way they did before we brought it in') states neither the new semantics nor the survival constraint concretely, so the agent must attribute the entangled code to its origin turns: the write-side normalization came from turn 3 and must go (probe: a tag typed 'API Design' must land in the file verbatim), while the case-insensitive search added in turn 5 must survive (probe: search 'devops' must still hit a note tagged 'DevOps' even though the word appears in no title or body). Because the code is on disk, a careful memoryless agent can reconstruct that attribution by reading store.py, so turn 6 discriminates by failure likelihood rather than solvability: an agent that lost the history is likelier to leave the write-side normalization in, or to rip the shared normalize helper out wholesale and take search's tag case-insensitivity down with it. The hard recall point is turn 8: turn 6 explicitly demands the cleanup logic be removed cleanly (no dead helper, docs/tests scrubbed), so after a compliant turn 6 the exact semantics exist nowhere in the workspace, and turn 8 ('bring back that normalization behavior ... exactly the way it used to') never restates them — the agent must recall lowercase + strip + collapse-internal-whitespace-runs-to-'-' from the conversation alone (probes: 'My  Tag ' -> 'my-tag', ' Deep   Work ' -> 'deep-work'; per-space replacement would give 'deep---work', and the turn-6 anecdote 'API Design' -> 'api-design' leaks lowercase+dash but not strip or run-collapse, so neither substitutes for the turn-3 spec). A growing-transcript agent has turns 3 and 5 in-window by construction; a bounded-slice agent must recall or page them in. Known limits: the oracle is final-state-only, so turn-6 removal compliance — and therefore the turn-8 recall guarantee — is prompted but not independently verified (an agent that keeps the helper on disk at turn 6 weakens turn 8 to a code read), and an agent that silently skips the net-no-op turn 3+6 pair is indistinguishable in the final state; the pair's only surviving trace is that turn 8's probes require turn 3's exact spec.
